source.title: Learning Curves for Analysis of Deep Networks
source.authors: D. Hoiem; Tanmay Gupta; Zhizhong Li; Michal Shlapentokh-Rothman

record.file_problem: The full paper and appendix are present. Some figures and tables are flattened in the text, but the relevant values are identifiable.
record.tranche_reason: The study applies learning-curve fitting to image-classification models and reports results, extending curve-form analysis to a different modality. It does not test language-model pretraining loss or parameter/token/compute scaling.
record.gate_note: The study measures image-classification test error against training-set size, not language-model held-out cross-entropy against parameters, tokens, or compute. Its image learning-curve experiments bear on V5 and its fitting-sensitivity findings bear partly on V7. References to Kaplan et al. and other prior work are not study results.
record.test_reason: The study fits an extended power law, error = α + ηn^γ, to image-classifier test error against training-set size. It reports fit quality, held-out prediction and how the exponent varies with setup. This tests V5 in a new modality, including fine-tuning and transfer, and bears on V7's point that fits depend on setup and fitting choices, here in a vision setting. It does not study language-model loss, parameter or compute scaling, or compute-optimal allocation.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly correct. The authors conclude that the extended power law fits image-classifier learning curves well, but its parameters α, η and γ are individually unstable. They therefore propose reporting eN and βN, which are stable, can be estimated from few trained models, and reveal design differences that single-size comparisons hide. They note that very small training sets deviate from the model.
record.recipe_differences: The study fits test classification error against training examples for convolutional image classifiers. It does not measure language-model cross-entropy against parameter count, tokens, or compute, and does not study compute-optimal allocation.
record.method_sensitivity: Fit parameterization and weighting affect prediction performance; fitted α, η, and γ can be unstable under measurement perturbations; fitted γ varies across datasets, models, and optimization settings; very small training sizes can depart from the curve form.
record.problems: The evidence concerns image-classification error rather than language-model pretraining loss. The paper itself notes instability of α, η, and γ under measurement perturbations and deviations at very small training sizes. Some numeric comparisons are presented in flattened figures and tables.
record.rows_left_out: Other separately plotted learning-curve results, including pretraining and fine-tuning comparisons, pretraining sources, depth/width/ensemble comparisons, and data augmentation, are not itemized here. The included rows emphasize the curve-form validation, fit sensitivity, architecture examples, and optimizer examples relevant to V5 and V7.

untested.parts: Cross-entropy loss rather than classification error; scaling in parameters or compute; ranges spanning several orders of magnitude (only 25–400 per class fitted, 1600 for held-out extrapolation); video, repeated data.
Parameter-counting conventions, training-schedule effects on compute-optimal splits, and disagreement between published language-model scaling laws.
Not tested: no language-model pretraining loss.
Only a 4x extrapolation (n=1600) in vision; no LM runs orders of magnitude larger.
Not tested for LMs; the depth/width results concern data-reliance of CNNs at different parameter counts.

missing.what: Comparison of the fixed γ=−0.5 three-point fit with the full fit: similar e400 and β400 (RMS diff 0.42 / 0.95). This is evidence on how sensitive the fit is to fitting choices.
Pretraining/fine-tuning and pretraining-source learning curves, with γ from −0.24 to −0.84 depending on transfer setup. V5 explicitly names fine-tuning and transfer.
Held-out extrapolation to n=1600 on Places365 from fits to n≤400.
Fits on additional datasets (Caltech101, Pets, Sun397) with γ effectively at the prior value −0.5.
Authors speculate γ is set mainly by hyperparameters and optimization rather than model design.
missing.locator: Section 5, Cause and impact of γ

record.verdict_notes: This is a vision data-scaling study, not an LM study. Its relevance to the claim is limited to V5 (other modality, fine-tuning, transfer) and to V7 by analogy. The fitted range is narrow, about 16x in n. The γ search uses an L1 prior pulling toward −0.5, which biases fitted exponents. Table 3 inconsistently writes ηn^−γ.

versions.untested_parts: Language-model held-out pretraining loss as a function of parameters, tokens, or compute.
Prediction of language-model loss for runs orders of magnitude larger; the study's prediction experiments concern vision classification error and training-set size.
Compute-optimal parameter and token allocation and how either scales with compute.
Architecture effects on language-model loss at fixed parameter count.

Video models, repeated data, fine-tuning or transfer as extensions of language-model pretraining loss, and whether the same form holds for cross-entropy loss. The experiments instead fit image-classification error against training-set size.
Downstream-task performance predicted from language-model scale or pretraining loss.

Parameter-count conventions, compute-optimal splits, and disagreement between published language-model scaling laws. The study does examine sensitivity of vision learning-curve fits to parameterization and measurement perturbations.

rows.subject: 16 Cifar100 classifiers with varying design decisions
rows.operation_detail: Fit and evaluate image-classification learning curves over training-set sizes using leave-one-size-out prediction.
rows.value: The proposed model achieved R2 of 0.998; the authors describe the fit as very good.
rows.note: This is image classification error versus training examples, not language-model loss versus model scale.
rows.check: Value is right: R2 = 0.998 and average leave-one-size-out RMSE of 1.04 for the α,η,γ model with the proposed weights. The range is only 25–400 samples per class, about 1.2 orders of magnitude.

rows.subject: Cifar100 learning-curve model comparison
rows.operation_detail: Compare alternative parameterizations for fitting learning curves.

conditions.value: α + ηn^γ versus special cases of α + ηn^γ + δn^(2γ)

rows.value: The authors report that their α + ηn^γ model outperforms the other parameterizations in most cases, often with high significance.
rows.note: The paper also reports high covariance and instability of α, η, and γ under small data perturbations.
rows.check: State should be observed, not partial. The extended power law beats its special cases (avg RMSE 1.04 vs 1.16–1.42), and the choice of parameterization and weighting changes prediction error. That is the fit-dependence V7 names.

source_check.locator_found: Section 4.1, Model Choice; Figure 2: average RMSE 1.04 versus 1.16, 1.30 and 1.42 for alternative parameterizations.

rows.subject: Resnet-18, no pretraining, fine-tuned, tested on Places365
rows.operation_detail: Repeatedly fit curves from four resampled measurements, one each at n = 50, 100, 200, and 400.
rows.measure: Stability of fitted eN, βN, and γ, and extrapolation
rows.value: The preferred model extrapolated best to n = 1600 and n = 25 and retained stable eN and βN estimates; estimated asymptotic error α varied widely.
rows.uncertainty: Standard deviations of estimates are shown in parentheses in the figure legend; numerical values not stated in the text.
rows.note: The authors describe curve estimates as stable in some summaries but report wide variation in α.
rows.check: For V7 this is observed: the fitted asymptotic error α varies widely under resampled measurements, while eN and βN stay stable. The std values are only in the Fig. 9 legend and are not readable from the flattened text.

source_check.locator_found: Section 4.1, Model Stability; Appendix B.2; Figure 9 and caption.

rows.subject: Image-classification learning curves at very small training sizes
rows.operation_detail: Compare fitted learning-curve behavior across training-set sizes.
rows.measure: Fit to the extended power-law learning-curve model
rows.value: The authors state that sizes smaller than 25 samples per class are strongly influenced by bounded error and deviate from the model.
rows.locator: Appendix A, Number of Training Examples; Section 5, Small training sets
rows.note: This is a stated limit on the image-classification learning-curve fit.
rows.check: This is a stated deviation below 25 samples per class, not a measured value. For V5 the power-law form fails in that regime. For V7 it is an instance of the curve bending away from a single power law.

relationships.condition: CNN image classifiers (Cifar100, Cifar10, Places365), fine-tuned or from scratch, 25–400 samples per class
relationships.reason: The extended power law fits with R2 0.998 and low leave-one-size-out RMSE (R1, R2), and it gives well-fitting curves across architectures and optimizers (R5–R17).
relationships.display_finding: The extended power law achieved R² = 0.998 on Cifar100 with low leave-one-size-out RMSE and fit curves across architectures and optimizers.

source_check.label: supports
source_check.condition: CNN image classifiers (Cifar100, Cifar10, Places365), fine-tuned or from scratch, 25–400 samples per class
source_check.reason: Support is warranted, but the shared training-size condition is inaccurate. Appendix A gives 25–400 samples per class for Cifar100 and includes 1600 for Places365; Section 4.2 and Figure 4 use N = 4000 for Cifar10. Separate these dataset conditions. Figure 2 reports R² = 0.998 for the preferred Cifar100 fit.

relationships.condition: Very small training sets (<25 samples per class)
relationships.reason: The authors state that error at these sizes is dominated by bounded error and deviates from the power-law form (R4).
relationships.display_finding: Bounded error dominated at these training-set sizes, producing departures from the power-law form.

relationships.condition: Vision data-scaling fits across optimizers, pretraining, architectures and parameterizations
relationships.reason: Fitted γ ranges from −0.21 to −0.84 across setups, and γ shifts with the optimizer (R10–R17). Parameterization and weighting change prediction error (R2). Fitted α is unstable under resampling (R3).
relationships.display_finding: Fitted γ ranges from −0.21 to −0.84 and changes with optimizer choice, while parameterization and weighting alter prediction error and fitted α is unstable under resampling.

source_check.label: supports

The broader −0.84 to −0.21 range occurs across other setups in Figures 5 and 7 and Table 3, not R10–R17 alone. relationships.condition: Derived summaries eN, βN rather than raw exponents

relationships.display_finding: Fixing γ at −0.5 and fitting three sizes produced similar e400 and β400 summaries, with reported RMS differences of 0.42 and 0.95.

source_check.reason: V7 concerns fitted exponents and compute-optimal splits, not instability of every derived summary. Similar e400 and β400 under fixed-γ fitting does not limit that claim. Appendix D also reports two RMS differences, 0.42 and 0.95, rather than 0.42 for both.

tranche.reason: Own experiments test power-law data scaling in CNN image classification, including pretraining and fine-tuning, extending the setting beyond language-model pretraining.

source_check.notes: Experimental errors use held-out validation partitions rather than official benchmark test sets. Table 3's exponent sign and Appendix D's γ400 notation are inconsistent with the main text; the listed figure values remain readable and consistent.

statements.correction: Section 4.1 and Appendix D: fixing γ = −0.5 and fitting the three largest training sizes yields similar e400 and β400. Appendix D reports RMS differences 0.42 and 0.95, respectively, although it prints γ400 for the second summary. Stable derived summaries do not establish stable fitted exponents or compute-optimal allocations.
statements.problem: The factual statement about stable derived summaries is correct, but treating it as evidence against V7 extends V7 beyond its stated scope of fitted exponents and compute-optimal allocation.
